business.exports.sli.ledeRead: What the exporter tells its forwarder, from which the bill of lading is drafted: each signed version, exactly as it was signed.
business.exports.sli.stale: The export changed since version {n} was signed — the weight, the box, its seal or the booking. Sign it again, so your forwarder has the letter as it is now.
business.exports.sli.onTheLine: Filled in and signed in the letter of instruction below.
business.exports.sli.fromExport: From the export: {shipper} as the shipper, to {forwarder}, booking {booking} — with the vessel, the port, the box, its seal and its weight.
business.exports.sli.shipperContact: Who the forwarder asks about it (a name, a phone)
business.exports.sli.kind.to_order_of_ba: To the order of a bank
business.exports.sli.bank: The bank it is made out to the order of
business.exports.sli.goodsHint: As the bill of lading should read them. The HS code is yours, as on your invoice: SeeBuyGet does not classify goods.
business.exports.sli.letterOfCredit: Letter of credit number (if paid by one)
business.exports.sli.saved: The draft is saved. Nothing reaches your forwarder until it is signed.
business.exports.sli.signedNote: Signed as version {n}, and kept exactly as it is. Hand it to your forwarder; your clearing agent is told.
business.exports.sli.signHint: Version {n} was signed on {when}. Signing again makes a new version; version {n} stays as it was.
business.exports.sli.goodsFromPacking: Worked out from your packing list — one line for each description, HS code and kind of package. Change the packing list to change them.
business.exports.packing.title: Packing list
business.exports.packing.lede: Bring in the packing list from your own file — the one your system already makes. Every line is kept, with any column of your own; your letter of instruction’s goods are worked out from it. Signed, it is kept exactly as signed.
business.exports.packing.ledeRead: The exporter’s packing list, from its own file: each signed version, exactly as it was signed.
business.exports.packing.more: And {n, plural, one {# more line} other {# more lines}} — preview the whole list to see every one.
business.exports.packing.signedNote: Signed as version {n}, and kept exactly as it is. Your clearing agent is told.
business.exports.packing.fileHint: A workbook from Excel (.xlsx) or a CSV file, as your system exports it — the heading rows above your table and a total row at the end are passed by.
business.exports.packing.pasteLabel: Copy the rows in your spreadsheet, headings included, and paste them here
business.exports.packing.ownSystem: Your own system can send it with your business’s key, without anybody typing it: see the systems page.
business.exports.packing.read: Read: {totals}. Its headings were found on row {row}.
business.exports.packing.columnsHint: Change any that was read wrong. What you choose is remembered for your business: your next file is read the same way. A column we have no field for is kept and printed as it is.
business.exports.packing.because.heading: By its heading
business.exports.packing.converted: Converted from {from}, as its heading says.
business.exports.packing.problems: {n, plural, one {# line cannot} other {# lines cannot}} be kept as {n, plural, one {it is} other {they are}} — put the file right, or match the columns, and check it again:
business.exports.packing.import: Bring in {n, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}
business.exports.packing.importedNote: {n, plural, one {# line is} other {# lines are}} on the export. Sign the list when it is right.
business.exports.packing.onTheLine: Brought in and signed under “Packing list” below — or attach your own.
business.exports.invoice.title: Commercial invoice
business.exports.invoice.lede: Drawn from your packing list’s lines and prices, so the invoice, the list and the letter cannot disagree. The core is the same everywhere; add what the destination asks for — particulars by their own names, declarations in its own words. What you add is remembered for your next invoice to the same country.
business.exports.invoice.ledeRead: The exporter’s commercial invoice, drawn from its packing list: each signed version, exactly as it was signed.
business.exports.invoice.stale: Your packing list changed since version {n} was signed. Sign the invoice again, so it says what the list says.
business.exports.invoice.totals: {lines, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} from your packing list · goods {goods} · total {total}
business.exports.invoice.fromTemplate: Started from your last invoice with {country} as its destination ({code}): its particulars’ names, its declarations and its terms. Change anything that does not fit this one.
business.exports.invoice.terms.lc_sight: Letter of credit, payable at sight
business.exports.invoice.termsOther: The payment terms, in your words
business.exports.invoice.buyerTax: Its tax or import number, as its country knows it
business.exports.invoice.consigneeIsBuye: The buyer is the consignee (otherwise, as your letter of instruction names it)
business.exports.invoice.chargesHint: Freight, insurance, inland haulage — whatever your trade term puts on this invoice, by name. A discount is an amount below zero.
business.exports.invoice.particularsHint: Particulars by their own names — the buyer’s import number, an order number, a licence. Every country asks its own; one you leave empty is kept but not printed. They are remembered for your next invoice there.
business.exports.invoice.declarationsHin: Every invoice declares itself true — that sentence is below. Add any statement the destination wants in its own words, an origin statement for instance; it is remembered for your next invoice there.
business.exports.invoice.columns: Your list’s own columns to print on the invoice
business.exports.invoice.saved: The invoice is saved. Nothing reaches anyone until it is signed.
business.exports.invoice.signedNote: Signed as version {n}, and kept exactly as it is. What it carried for this country is remembered for your next invoice there.
business.exports.invoice.onTheLine: Drawn from your packing list and signed under “Commercial invoice” below — or attach your own.
business.exports.papers.entryPh: The entry number from your clearing agent
business.exports.papers.saved: The paper is on the export.
business.exports.laden.title: To the terminal
business.exports.laden.hint: Post the load to the terminal once the box is stuffed: a driver sees the gate cut-off and your booking. Give its weight, or declare the verified gross mass first.
business.exports.laden.hintRail: Post the load to {terminal} once the box is stuffed: a driver sees the train’s cut-off and your booking. Give its weight, or declare the verified gross mass first.
business.exports.laden.hintRailVgm: Post the load to {terminal} once the box is stuffed: a driver sees the train’s cut-off and your booking, and its weight is the verified gross mass.
business.exports.laden.dangerousHint: These goods are declared dangerous: give their UN number, proper shipping name and class, from the safety data sheet. The consignment note prints them, and the driver needs them.
business.exports.laden.hintVgm: Post the load to the terminal once the box is stuffed: a driver sees the gate cut-off and your booking, and its weight is the verified gross mass.
business.exports.laden.post: Post the load to the terminal
business.exports.laden.posted: The load to the terminal is posted for a driver.
business.exports.laden.sealIt: Write the seal on load {code} under Domestic › Loads, with its three photographs, before the driver collects it.
business.exports.laden.none: No load to the terminal yet.
business.exports.handover.title: For your forwarder at the gate
business.exports.handover.hint: One file with the booking, the cut-offs, the box, its seal, its weight, the papers and the road consignment note — what is still missing is marked.
business.exports.bl.label: Bill of lading number, once issued
business.exports.bl.saved: The bill of lading number is recorded.
business.exports.agentLede: As a clearing agent you see here the exports a business appointed you on: read the papers attached, give the export entry, and accept each paper or send it back with a reason.
business.exports.noneAgent: No exports yet. When a business appoints you as its clearing agent on one, it shows here and in your bell.
business.exports.clock.title: The box’s clock
business.exports.clock.unknown: No clock runs on the box yet: as far as anyone has recorded, the empty has not left the depot.
business.exports.clock.outside.noClaim: Outside the terminal (detention) since {since}: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Say how many free days the line gives, to count to a date.
business.exports.clock.outside.running: Outside the terminal (detention) since {since}: day {day} of the {free} free days {by} gave. It must be inside the gate by {due}.
business.exports.clock.outside.over: The {free} free days outside the terminal (detention) ran out on {due}, {over, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago. Each day over is the line’s to charge, under your agreement with it.
business.exports.clock.inside.noClaim: Inside the terminal (demurrage) since {since}: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Say how many free days it may wait there, to count to a date.
business.exports.clock.inside.running: Inside the terminal (demurrage) since {since}: day {day} of the {free} free days {by} gave. It must be loaded on board by {due}.
business.exports.clock.inside.over: The {free} free days inside the terminal (demurrage) ran out on {due}, {over, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago. Ask your forwarder about the vessel, and record it loaded once it is.
business.exports.clock.stopped: Loaded on board: the box’s clock has stopped. It was {outside, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} outside the terminal and {inside, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} inside.
business.exports.clock.tagSoon: Free days end in {n, plural, =0 {less than a day} one {# day} other {# days}}
business.exports.clock.claim: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, said by {by} on {when}
business.exports.clock.hint: The free days are in your agreement with the line or your forwarder: write them here and the clock counts to a date, and you are told three days before it. Days only — what a day over costs is between you and the line. Times are in UTC, as everywhere on SeeBuyGet.
business.exports.clock.saved: The free days are saved. A new figure replaces the old one; both stay on the record.
business.exports.clock.emptyOutLabel: When the empty left the depot
business.exports.clock.emptyOutSaved: The empty’s leaving is recorded: the clock outside the terminal counts from it.
business.exports.clock.loadedLabel: When it was loaded on board
business.exports.clock.loadedSaved: Loaded on board: the box’s clock has stopped.
business.exports.agent.title: Clearing agent
business.exports.agent.none: No clearing agent is appointed. Appoint one to read this export’s papers, give you the export entry, and accept each paper or send it back.
business.exports.agent.appointed: {name} is appointed, since {when} (by {by}). It reads the papers attached here, and nothing else of yours.
business.exports.agent.youAre: {exporter} appointed you as its clearing agent on {when}. Read the papers attached, give the export entry, and accept each paper or send it back with a reason.
business.exports.agent.appointedNote: {name} is appointed and told. It can read this export’s papers now.
business.exports.agent.seen: We have seen {appointed, plural, one {# appointment} other {# appointments}} and {cleared} cleared.
business.exports.agent.new: New here — nothing to show yet, which is not the same as a bad record.
business.exports.f.ownBox: The box is ours (we own it), not lent by the shipping line
business.exports.clock.owned: The box is yours: no shipping line lent it, so no line’s free days run on it and no clock counts.
business.exports.clock.ownerLine: The shipping line’s, lent for this booking
business.exports.clock.lineBox: The box is the line’s after all
business.exports.clock.ownSaved: Saved: the box is yours, and no line’s clock runs on it.
business.exports.clock.lineSaved: Saved: the box is the line’s, and its clock counts again.
business.exports.fee.title: Its fee
business.exports.fee.none: {name} has not quoted its fee yet. You are told when it does.
business.exports.fee.noneAgent: Quote your fee for clearing this export. The exporter is told and agrees to it here; SeeBuyGet moves no money between you.
business.exports.fee.agreeHint: Agree if this is the figure you agreed with your agent. Agreeing is not paying.
business.exports.fee.hint: A quotation to the exporter, never a payment through SeeBuyGet. Left empty, the currency is that of the country the goods are sent from. A new figure asks the exporter to agree again.
business.exports.fee.sent: The quotation is sent, and the exporter is told.
business.exports.agent.basis: {n} listed, alphabetically. Not a ranking — each one says what it handles, beside what we have seen it do.
business.exports.agent.ended: {name}’s appointment has ended, and it is told. It no longer reads this export’s papers.
business.exports.agent.former: {n, plural, one {# earlier appointment} other {# earlier appointments}} on this export, kept on the record.
business.exports.papers.hintAgent: The exporter’s papers for this export. Open each one, then accept it or send it back with a reason the exporter can act on. The export entry is yours to give, by its number.
business.exports.papers.unreadable: {title} cannot be opened: it may have been replaced, or the appointment has ended.
business.exports.papers.refusedNote: Sent back. The exporter is told, with your reason.
business.exports.papers.entryGiven: The export entry is on the export, and the exporter is told.
business.clearing.title: Customs clearing
business.clearing.lede: Parcels sent abroad by SeeBuyGet arrive at its customs warehouse at the airport. Where you are named to clear, say what customs decided for each, and when a held one is paid. The parcel stays with the warehouse: released, it goes on to the receiver’s shop.
business.clearing.countries: Where you are named to clear
business.clearing.noCountries: SeeBuyGet has not named you to clear anywhere yet.
business.clearing.acceptOwner: An owner of the business accepts.
business.clearing.amount: What customs asks to be paid
business.clearing.lapsed: not paid in time: the sender is asked what to do
business.clearing.someoneElse: the sender named someone else to take it
business.clearing.givenUpLine: The warehouse hands it to customs to dispose of.
business.clearing.nothing: No parcel waits for you now.
business.inbound.title: Coming in
business.inbound.lede: What your suppliers send to your places, as it moves: your own order number, who it is from, how much, where it is now and who is bringing it. Never the price: that stays between you and your supplier.
business.inbound.pointsHint: Each place of yours that receives has a code. Give it to your suppliers: when they post a load on SeeBuyGet, they write it under “Deliver to”, and the load comes to that place and shows here. The code tells them the place and nothing else of yours.
business.inbound.noPlaces: Add a place of your own under Business details first: a yard, a store, a factory gate.
business.inbound.openDone: {place} receives goods now: give its code to your suppliers.
business.inbound.shareText: To send to {business} at {place} with SeeBuyGet, write this code under “Deliver to” when you post the load: {code}
business.inbound.copied: The code for {place}, with how to use it, is copied: paste it to your supplier.
business.inbound.newCodeDone: {place} has a new code. The old one names nothing from now: give the new one to your suppliers.
business.inbound.closedDone: {place} no longer receives through SeeBuyGet. What was already sent there still shows below.
business.inbound.pastTitle: Arrived or withdrawn, the last fortnight
business.inbound.noneComing: Nothing is on its way to you just now.
business.inbound.noneYet: Nothing yet. Once a place of yours receives, what your suppliers send there shows here.
business.inbound.waitingCarrier: Your supplier has posted it; no carrier has taken it yet.
business.inbound.collecting: A carrier has it and is on the way to collect it.
business.inbound.late: Running late against what was planned.
business.inbound.withdrawn: Your supplier withdrew it: it is not coming.
business.inbound.stillHint: Delivered, and not all as the note says. What did not come, or came and is not the goods, stays here until you close it: when it comes after all, or when you stop waiting for it.
business.inbound.stillLine: {n, plural, one {# package} other {# packages}} still expected
business.inbound.foundWithPhotos: Found at the handover: {found} ({n, plural, one {# photo} other {# photos}} on the note)
